AUTHOR: Park
TITLE: Fast cropping method for proper input size of convolutional neural networks in underwater photography
VENUE: JOURNAL OF THE SOCIETY FOR INFORMATION DISPLAY
REGION: South Korea (shallow stream / pond fish passage)
SPECIES: largemouth bass, bluegill, common carp, crucian carp, catfish, mandarin fish, skin carp (test: largemouth bass and bluegill only)
DATA: Own fixed camera in narrow pond/stream passage; training = 5000 synthetic images (lab fish images blended with natural noise images); test = 1000 pond images
V_EV: Sec. 1: 'The length of the passageway is 440 mm from the installed camera to the wall.'; Fig. 1 notes sunlight, lighting, floats
D_EV: Sec. 5: 'Each CNN is trained by 5000 images generated by synthesizing noise images with fish images taken in the experimental environment.'
R_EV: Sec. 5.2: 'We used 1000 images of largemouth bass and bluegill images taken over some months in the ponds (Figure 2B) for the testing images.'
C_EV: Sec. 5.2 (p.14): CNN species classification of cropped images evaluated by accuracy only ('classification performance ... for each CNN'); the only threshold is the brightness-difference ATD threshold for background subtraction (Sec. 3.1.2), not a score threshold -> NA
E_EV: Sec. 5.2: 'Figure 11 shows the results of a classification performance between the proposed method and the center-cropping method for each CNN.'
ARCH: Background-difference fish detection with adaptive threshold (two reference images) + line-based cropping; CNN classifiers AlexNet, VGG16, VGG19, GoogLeNet
METR: classification accuracy (Fig. 11), cropping time (6.7 ms), detection error rate (<1%)
NOTE: Eligibility borderline: test images from 'ponds' with camera in a narrow passage (abstract: 'cameras installed in a shallow stream'); not stated whether ponds are natural or aquaculture - verify. Training data is lab fish images synthesized with natural noise images, test is field pond images: coded D1 = 사이트/서식지 (separate acquisition environments, not a stated split) and R1 = Y (lab-to-field), but no in-domain test reported so R3 = N. C1/C_ALL based on the adaptive brightness threshold for the background-subtraction detection stage (modelled by least squares to give 99% detection), not a CNN confidence threshold; CNN classification itself has no reported score threshold. Accuracy values only in Fig. 11 (text: GoogLeNet +4.7% vs center crop). NIMG = 5000 synthetic training + 1000 test. V3 = Y from qualitative own-data statements on sunlight/illumination changes and brightness-based threshold; V4 = camera-to-wall 440 mm. PRE: 'transfer learning provided by Matlab', source dataset not named.
